posts.question: Who gets your good news first now, and who used to?
answers: Drifting has no one at the wheel. This protects you from saying who turned.
So are you, and the news still goes to someone. This protects the idea that it was their schedule.
“It's the same person it's always been.”
The fastest answer of the three. The last three pieces of good news would know. This protects the version where nothing has moved.
posts.caption:
Tuesday's question, read back. Three answers that come fast, and what each one tends to protect.

None of them is wrong. The point is which one you reached for first, and who it was standing in front of.
